No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. Never edit data/, docs/, .plans/, bench/. No story names (Kristin, drawer, truck, laptop...) in storygame/. Write tests first, run them and see them fail, then fix. List any existing test pin you change and why. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, tests/test_held_by_echo.py. BUG: in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py the held_by precedence block (~lines 1239-1305, 'held_by_wins') lets a narrator reply entry that restates a thing's CURRENT place and also adds held_by: protagonist move the thing into the protagonist's hands. Live evidence: the protagonist stood outside; the reply raw was {'Kristin': {'place': 'outside the house'}, "Kristin's laptop": {'place': 'on the passenger seat of Kristin\'s truck', 'held_by': 'Kristin', 'state': 'closed'}, 'passenger seat': {'place': "Kristin's truck"}, ...} for a plain look-around. The narration never mentions the laptop, but custody flipped to the protagonist, so the later boarding turn emitted no 'laptop sat on the passenger seat' notice. FIX (generic): when an entry's own place resolves to the thing's currently committed parent (an unchanged place) and the entry also has held_by naming someone other than that parent, the entry is self-contradictory; keep the committed place, drop held_by, still apply any condition/state fields of that entry. Genuine changes must still land (memory: a reply change that does not land is a severe failure): a held_by entry whose place is absent, or differs from the committed parent, or is the holder, behaves exactly as before, and engine-resolved takes (storygame/runtime/taking.py) are untouched. Do not parse prose; do not add regex. TESTS in tests/test_held_by_echo.py using a synthetic story (and, if cheap, the real raw above through the same capture entry point other item_facts tests use): echo with unchanged place keeps custody and still applies the state; a real pick-up (place = holder or omitted) still moves it; held_by with a different place from a different holder behaves as before. Look at existing tests/test_item_facts*.py for helpers. FINISH: ruff format and check touched files; run the focused tests you touched plus tests/test_held_by_echo.py tests/test_item_facts*.py tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py tests/test_world_capture*.py tests/test_taking*.py tests/test_boarding*.py.
